For the fourth quarter of 2025, consolidated revenue stood at 4.5 million euros, compared with 10.5 million euros in the fourth quarter of 2024, resulting in a net loss of 0.486 million euros against a net profit of 0.957 million euros in the prior-year period.

verified_key_information_units.information: The number of apartments handed over to customers decreased to 141 in 2025 (2024: 194), with 22 handed over in Q4 2025 (Q4 2024: 52), negatively impacting revenue and profitability.

candidate_sentences.text: The financial results were primarily affected by a decrease in the number of apartments handed over to customers, totaling 141 apartments in 2025 compared with 194 apartments in 2024.

verified_key_information_units.information: Primary sales agreements increased to 185 homes valued at 36.1 million euros in 2025 (2024: 109 homes and 19.8 million euros), driven by stable financial conditions and project supply expansion.

Profitability was pressured by a lower gross margin on sold projects (16.9% in 2025 vs 17.8% in 2024) and increased marketing expenses to 1.3 million euros (2024: 0.9 million euros), primarily due to larger project scales and intensified sales activities.

verified_key_information_units.information: A public bond offering was completed on 21 November 2025, increasing the volume from 6 million to 8 million euros (1.4 times oversubscribed) at a fixed annual interest rate of 9.50%, with the first interest payment scheduled for 26 February 2026.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report page 5; Main events page 19

candidate_sentences.text: In November 2025, the Group successfully completed a public bond issue raising 8.0 million euros at a fixed annual interest rate of 9.50%.

verified_key_information_units.information: The residential development portfolio expanded by six projects in 2025, adding approximately 700 planned apartments and 2,500 m² of commercial space, including the Manufaktuuri 3 site in Tallinn (planned for ~300 apartments) which allows for a high-rise building of up to 60 storeys.

As at 31 December 2025, the Group had 10 residential development projects on sale — 5 completed (355 homes, 327 sold, 28 unsold) and 5 under construction comprising 428 homes, a 223% increase from 192 homes at end-2024, with 227 homes under construction in Latvia and 201 in Estonia.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report page 6; Development projects under construction page 8

verified_key_information_units.information: Five new development projects are planned for launch in 2026: V7 residential (8 timber-frame apartments) and Paevälja quarter stage I (93 apartments, 918 m² commercial) in Estonia; Peetri business centre (3,551 m² leasable) in Estonia; Veidama quarter stage I (stock-office) and Starta 17 residential (255 apartments) in Latvia.

On 11 February 2026 (post-reporting period), a loan agreement of 5.25 million euros was signed with BluOr Bank for financing the construction of the Ķiršu Kalna Mājas residential development project in Riga.

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers K1 (revenue, net profit, Q4 figures and margins), K2 (apartment handovers), K4 (profitability pressures), and K5 (bond offering). However, it omits core material components for K3 (primary sales agreements), K6 (portfolio expansion details), K7 (project status breakdown), K8 (Toronto approval), K9 (2026 project plans), and K10 (loan agreement). These omissions include HIGH-importance data points that change the overall financial and operational picture. With only 4 out of 10 key information units adequately represented, the coverage is insufficient to qualify as generally yes.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements are logically connected and support each other without contradictions. The summary follows a clear structure: starting with consolidated financial results (revenue, net profit), then detailing quarterly performance, profitability drivers, balance sheet changes, cash flow, and concluding with an overall assessment. Explanations for changes in profitability (apartment handovers, margins, marketing expenses) logically support the reported financial metrics. There is no unnecessary repetition, and all relationships between figures and their explanations are clear and consistent within the document itself.
